---
title: "Your first dasviz figure"
guide-section: Tutorial
---

In this tutorial you install dasviz, draw a patch with it, and see what its namespaces hold. It takes about five minutes.

## Install

```bash
pip install dasviz
```

That brings DASCore if you don't have it. Nothing else is needed for figures; other backends are extras, covered in [Install backends](11-install-backends.qmd).

## Draw a waterfall

```python
import dascore as dc

patch = dc.get_example_patch()
ax = patch.fig.waterfall(scale=0.5)
```

You did not import dasviz. DASCore found the `fig` namespace through dasviz's entry point the first time you used it.

`waterfall` returns the matplotlib axes, so you can carry on with them, or pass your own with `ax=`. Large patches are decimated before drawing: each axis is cut to at most `max_samples` (2048) bins, each keeping its largest-magnitude sample, so spikes stay visible. The color limits always come from the full data.

## Look around

Each namespace says what it holds:

```python
>>> patch.fig
<dasviz 'fig' namespace on Patch: waterfall>
>>> patch.scene
<dasviz 'scene' namespace on Patch: patchviewer>
```

A spool has the same namespaces. A method which draws one patch points you to it:

```python
>>> spool = dc.get_example_spool()
>>> spool.fig.waterfall()
AttributeError: fig.waterfall draws a patch, and a spool is many of them. ...
```
